chosenAngle: How a new civilian space agency turned a tense space race moment into organized exploration, science, and engineering
episodeThesis: A public science agency can turn a big national challenge into missions that help people learn more about Earth, flight, and space.
timeline: July 29, 1958: President Dwight D. Eisenhower signs the National Aeronautics and Space Act
August 19, 1958: T. Keith Glennan and Hugh L. Dryden are sworn in as NASA's first administrator and deputy administrator
October 1, 1958: NASA officially begins operations as the United States' civilian space agency
storyBeats: A new agency opens for business while people are watching the space race closely
NASA brings together earlier aeronautics work from NACA with new space responsibilities
The first days of NASA show how exploration depends on teams, planning, and careful engineering
modernRelevance: Modern weather satellites, space telescopes, planetary probes, aviation research, and human spaceflight still depend on the kind of organized civilian science mission NASA began on October 1, 1958.

sources.title: NASA: 65 Years Ago: NASA Begins Operations
